title: Stuffed grape leaves with lamb and rice

content.title: About
content.content: Stuffed grape leaves with lamb and rice is a classic dish of Mediterranean and Middle Eastern cuisine. Thin grape leaves are wrapped around a savory filling of minced lamb, rice, onion and spices, then simmered in a tomato‑lemon broth.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The dish is known by many names – dolma, dolmades, sarma – across different countries.
Grape leaves are used not only in cooking but also in traditional medicine to aid digestion.
The original recipe is believed to have originated in the Ottoman Empire and spread throughout the Mediterranean.
While lamb is traditional, some regions substitute beef or chicken.
Slow cooking in the sauce makes the leaves tender and allows them to absorb all the flavors.

items.title: Rich source of protein
items.content: Lamb and rice provide a complete set of amino acids that support tissue growth and repair.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Lamb is a good source of heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: B‑vitamins
items.content: The dish supplies B12, B6 and niacin, which support nervous system function and metabolism.

items.title: Dietary fiber
items.content: Grape leaves and rice add fiber that promotes healthy digestion.

items.title: Antioxidants
items.content: Grape leaves are rich in polyphenols that help combat oxidative stress.

items.title: Meat allergy
items.content: Some individuals may be allergic to lamb or other meats.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: If prepared with brined leaves, the dish can be salty; monitor salt intake.

items.title: Digestive heaviness
items.content: A protein‑ and fiber‑rich meal may be heavy for people with sensitive stomachs.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: Serve the stuffed leaves warm or cold, often with a yogurt‑garlic sauce, lemon wedges or pomegranate seeds. They can be enjoyed as a main dish or as part of a mezze spread.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Keep cooked leaves in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 3‑4 days. For longer storage, freeze in portion‑sized bags – up to 2 months.
